theme: A person prepares for and attends their first in-person job interview after years of remote freelance work.
core_events: ["finds a promising job posting and submits an application", "gets invited to an in-person interview", "chooses an outfit and practices answers the night before", "travels to the office and completes the interview", "reflects on how it felt afterward"]
story_1_anchor: After several years of remote freelance work, Maya found a promising job posting for a full-time project coordinator. She submitted an application that afternoon. Two days later, she got invited to an in-person interview at the company office. The night before the meeting, she chose a simple navy outfit. She practiced her answers to common interview questions. The next morning, she traveled downtown to the office. She completed the interview with the hiring manager and a team lead. Afterward, she sat in a nearby cafe and reflected on how it felt. She felt nervous at first, but she was proud that she handled an in-person interview again.
story_2_similar: Lena had worked as a remote freelancer for years when she noticed a promising opening for an operations assistant. She sent in her application that evening. Later that week, the company invited her to an in-person interview. On the night before it, she picked out a clean blouse and dark pants. She practiced her responses out loud in her apartment. The next day, she took the train to the office. She completed the interview with steady answers and a few careful questions of her own. When it was over, she thought about the experience on the ride home. It had felt strange to be back in an office, but it also made her want a regular team job.
story_3_dissimilar: After years of taking freelance jobs from home, Erin wanted to try for a staff position. She found a promising job posting for an account support role. She submitted an application and then spent several days wondering if she still remembered office life. Soon, she received an invitation to come in for an in-person interview. On the evening before the visit, she practiced answers at her kitchen table. She chose her outfit only after changing her mind twice. In the morning, she traveled across town to the office building. She completed the interview and noticed that speaking face to face took more energy than video calls. Afterward, she reflected on how it felt while walking to the bus stop. She was tired and unsure, but she was glad she had shown up.

theme: A person adopts a dog from a local shelter and adjusts to the first week together.
core_events: ["visits the animal shelter to look at dogs", "decides to adopt one dog and completes the paperwork", "brings the dog home and introduces it to the space", "handles an early challenge like barking or an accident", "settles into a small routine with the dog"]
story_1_anchor: On Saturday, Mia went to the local animal shelter to look at dogs. She met a calm brown dog that stayed close to her. She decided to adopt him and filled out the paperwork at the front desk. That afternoon, she brought the dog home. She walked him through the living room and kitchen so he could see the space. The first night, he barked when he heard sounds outside. Mia sat with him and waited until he settled down. By the end of the week, they had a small routine. She fed him at the same times each day and took him on short walks in the morning.
story_2_similar: On a weekend morning, Jordan visited a nearby shelter to look at the dogs. One small black dog followed him along the kennel door. He chose that dog and completed the adoption forms with the staff. Later, he took the dog back to his apartment. He let the dog sniff each room and rest near the couch. On the second day, the dog had an accident on the floor. Jordan cleaned it up and took the dog outside right away. After a few days, they started a simple routine. Jordan gave meals on a schedule and went out for a walk before work.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena spent part of her week at a local shelter looking at several dogs. She kept thinking about a shy white dog after she left. The next day, she returned and signed the paperwork to adopt that dog. At home, the first challenge came early. The dog barked at the bedroom door during the night. Lena stayed nearby until the dog became quiet. In the morning, she showed the dog the rooms one by one. By the end of the first week, they were getting used to each other. Lena opened the back door at the same times each day and set regular feeding times.

theme: A college student struggles through and eventually finishes a major group presentation.
core_events: ["gets assigned to a group project in class", "meets with the group and divides the tasks", "deals with a setback such as a missing section or disagreement", "rehearses the presentation shortly before class", "delivers the presentation to the class"]
story_1_anchor: Maya got assigned to a group project in her history class. She felt nervous because the presentation counted for a large part of her grade. She met with her group in the library. The group divided the tasks between the members. Maya took the introduction and the final slides. Two days before class, Maya found that one section was missing from the shared file. She messaged the group and felt stressed about the problem. The group fixed the missing section that night. On the morning of the presentation, they rehearsed in an empty classroom. Maya stumbled over her lines during practice. She took a breath and tried again. Later that day, Maya delivered the presentation to the class with her group. She was shaky at first, but she finished her part.
story_2_similar: Jordan was assigned to a group project in his sociology course. He worried because speaking in class was hard for him. He met his teammates after class. They split the work into separate parts. Jordan agreed to cover the opening and one example. The evening before the presentation, he noticed that a teammate had not added a key section. He sent a message to the group and got frustrated. The missing part was completed after a quick discussion. Right before class, the group rehearsed in the hallway. Jordan forgot one sentence during the run-through. He checked his notes and practiced it again. When class began, Jordan delivered the presentation to the class with the others. His voice was quiet, but he made it to the end.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena was assigned to a group project in her biology class. She immediately worried about working with people she did not know well. She met with the group later that week. The members divided the tasks after a short discussion. Lena prepared the data section for the slides. On the day of the presentation, she still felt unsure about her part. Shortly before class, the group rehearsed in a study room. During practice, two members disagreed about the order of the slides. The disagreement slowed them down and made Lena more anxious. They adjusted the slide order and moved on. A few minutes later, Lena delivered the presentation to the class with her group. She spoke too fast at first, but she finished the talk.

theme: A person plans a surprise birthday dinner for their sibling.
core_events: ["decides to organize a surprise dinner", "contacts family or friends and chooses a restaurant or location", "comes up with a reason to bring the sibling there", "waits for the sibling to arrive while everyone hides or gathers", "reveals the surprise and celebrates together"]
story_1_anchor: Maya decided to organize a surprise birthday dinner for her brother. She called their parents and a few close friends. She picked a small Italian restaurant near his apartment. She told her brother that she needed help meeting a friend there. Everyone arrived early and waited inside. They stayed quiet until her brother walked in. Then they jumped up and shouted, "Surprise!" They ate dinner together and celebrated his birthday.
story_2_similar: Lena chose to plan a surprise birthday dinner for her sister. She texted family members and invited two of her sister's friends. She reserved a table at a Mexican restaurant downtown. She told her sister that they were going there for a quick meal after work. The guests gathered before her sister got there. They waited by the table and tried not to be seen. When her sister entered, they revealed the surprise. After that, everyone shared dinner and celebrated together.
story_3_dissimilar: Noah wanted to do something special for his sister's birthday, so he planned a surprise dinner. At first he thought about cooking at home. Then he asked cousins and friends to join the plan. He chose their aunt's house instead of a restaurant. He told his sister that he needed to drop off a package there. The family spent time setting out food and decorations. Some guests were still arriving when his sister came to the door. Noah opened the door and the group greeted her with cheers. She laughed, and they celebrated with dinner together.

theme: A person deals with a phone that stops working on an important day.
core_events: ["notices the phone malfunctioning or refusing to turn on", "tries basic fixes like charging or restarting it", "realizes the phone problem interferes with plans for the day", "visits a repair shop or contacts support", "ends the day with a temporary or final solution"]
story_1_anchor: On the morning of her job interview, Mia pressed her phone's power button and nothing happened. She plugged it into the charger and waited a few minutes. She tried to restart it again, but the screen stayed black. She then realized she could miss the interview messages and the map to the office. She went to a phone repair shop near the train station. The technician could not fully fix it right away, but he got it to turn on for a short time. Mia wrote down her directions and ended the day using the phone carefully until she could replace it.
story_2_similar: Early on the day of his final exam, Daniel noticed that his phone would not turn on. He connected it to a charger and watched for any sign of power. He held the buttons to force a restart, but it still did not respond. He realized the broken phone could make him miss messages from his class group and his ride home. He contacted customer support and then stopped by a repair store after the exam. The shop gave him a loaner phone for the evening, and that was his temporary solution for the day.
story_3_dissimilar: Sara woke up on the day of her sister's wedding and saw that her phone was frozen and then shut off. She first worried about how she would coordinate with her family without it. She borrowed a charger and tried to power the phone back up. She attempted a restart several times, but nothing changed. After the ceremony, she visited a repair counter at the mall. The worker said the battery had failed and ordered a new one. Sara ended the day using her cousin's old phone until the repair was done.

theme: A person trains for and completes their first 10K race.
core_events: ["signs up for a local 10K race", "starts a training routine over several weeks", "faces a discouraging run or minor obstacle during training", "arrives at the race and lines up at the start", "finishes the race and reacts to the result"]
story_1_anchor: Maya signed up for a local 10K race at the park. She began a training routine and ran three times a week for several weeks. One evening, she had a hard run and felt discouraged when she had to stop early. She rested the next day and then returned to her plan. On race morning, she arrived at the event and lined up at the start. She finished the race and felt proud of completing her first 10K.
story_2_similar: Ethan registered for a local 10K race in his town. He started a training plan and practiced for several weeks. During one workout, he felt sore and upset because the run went badly. He took an easier day and kept training after that. On the day of the race, he got to the course and stood at the starting line. He completed the race and was happy with the result.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena signed up for her first local 10K after thinking about it for months. Before race day, she followed a training routine for several weeks. At first, the schedule felt exciting. Later, she twisted her ankle slightly during a training run and worried she would not be ready. She still went to the race and lined up at the start with nervous energy. She finished the 10K more slowly than she hoped. Even so, she felt relieved and proud when she crossed the line.

theme: A person takes a weekend trip alone to a nearby city for the first time.
core_events: ["books transportation and a place to stay", "travels to the city and checks in", "explores a landmark, neighborhood, or museum alone", "encounters a small problem like getting lost or changing plans", "returns home thinking about the solo trip"]
story_1_anchor: On Thursday, Maya decided to spend the weekend alone in a nearby city for the first time. She booked a train ticket online. She reserved a small room in a budget hotel. On Saturday morning, she took the train to the city. She walked from the station to the hotel. She checked in at the front desk. After lunch, she visited the city art museum by herself. She spent an hour looking at the paintings in silence. Later, she took a wrong turn in an unfamiliar neighborhood. She stopped and checked a map on her phone. She found the right street after a few minutes. On Sunday evening, she rode the train back home. During the trip home, she thought about how calm and proud she felt after traveling alone.
story_2_similar: Ethan wanted to try a solo weekend in a nearby city for the first time. On Friday, he bought a bus ticket. He also booked one night in a simple guesthouse. The next morning, he rode the bus to the city. He carried his bag to the guesthouse. He checked in with the owner. In the afternoon, he explored a famous old market alone. He walked slowly and looked at the small shops. Later, a street he planned to use was closed for a parade. He changed his route and followed a different road. The new path took longer, but he reached the center safely. On Sunday, he returned home by bus. On the ride back, he kept thinking about the freedom of doing the trip by himself.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena chose a nearby city for her first weekend trip alone. She reserved a seat on a regional bus. She booked a bed in a hostel for one night. Early on Saturday, she packed lightly for the short trip. She traveled to the city after breakfast. She checked in when she reached the hostel. Soon after that, she wandered through a historic neighborhood by herself. She spent more time there than she expected. She missed the time slot she wanted for a museum visit. She decided to skip the museum and sit in a cafe instead. On Sunday afternoon, she went back home. While returning, she thought about what she learned from being alone in a new place.

theme: A person learns to cook one meaningful family recipe from an older relative.
core_events: ["asks the relative to teach the recipe", "shops for the ingredients together or from a list", "follows the cooking steps in the kitchen", "makes or fixes a mistake during the process", "sits down to taste the finished dish"]
story_1_anchor: Maya asked her grandmother to teach her the family dumpling soup recipe. Her grandmother wrote a short list for the broth, dough, and filling. Maya went with her to the market and bought the ingredients. Back in the kitchen, Maya chopped the vegetables. She mixed the dough and rolled it flat. She filled the dumplings and dropped them into the soup. She added too much salt to the pot. Her grandmother told her to add more water and a cut potato to soften the taste. Maya fixed the soup and let it simmer. Then they sat down together and tasted the finished dish.
story_2_similar: Lena asked her aunt to show her how to make the family cabbage rolls. Her aunt gave her a list of meat, rice, cabbage, and tomato sauce. Lena followed the list at the grocery store and bought everything. At home, Lena stood beside her aunt in the kitchen. She cooked the rice and softened the cabbage leaves. She mixed the filling and rolled each leaf around it. She tore two leaves because she pulled too hard. Her aunt showed her how to wrap the next ones more gently. Lena finished the tray and baked it. After that, they sat at the table and tasted the dish.
story_3_dissimilar: Noah wanted to learn his grandfather's bean stew, so he asked him for the recipe. His grandfather first told him the order of the steps from memory. Noah copied down a list of beans, onions, garlic, carrots, and sausage. Noah shopped alone and brought the ingredients to his grandfather's house. In the kitchen, his grandfather asked him to soak the beans and cut the vegetables. Noah put the pot on high heat and the bottom began to scorch. They moved the stew to a clean pot and lowered the flame. His grandfather had Noah add the sausage near the end. They tasted a spoonful while it cooked. Later, they sat down and ate the finished stew together.

theme: A person starts therapy and reflects on the first appointment.
core_events: ["decides to look for a therapist", "books a first appointment after some hesitation", "arrives for the session and discusses why they came", "responds to a question or topic that feels unexpectedly difficult", "leaves the appointment and thinks about whether to continue"]
story_1_anchor: After feeling overwhelmed for months, Maya decided to look for a therapist. She read several profiles online and saved two names. She hesitated for a few days before making contact. Then she booked a first appointment for the following week. On the day of the visit, she arrived early and sat in the waiting room. When the session started, she explained that stress and low mood had pushed her to come. A little later, the therapist asked about her family. Maya found that question unexpectedly hard to answer. She paused for a long moment and felt tears come up. After the appointment ended, she walked home slowly. She thought about whether she wanted to continue therapy. By the time she reached her apartment, she felt unsure but willing to try one more session.
story_2_similar: Jonah reached a point where he decided to look for a therapist. He searched clinic websites and compared a few options. He almost closed the booking page twice because he felt nervous. After that hesitation, he booked a first appointment. A week later, he arrived for the session a little early. Once inside the office, he talked about anxiety at work and trouble sleeping. During the conversation, the therapist asked him when he last felt safe. The question caught him off guard and was hard to answer. He stared at the floor before saying anything. When the visit was over, he stepped outside and took a slow walk. He thought about whether to continue. In the end, he decided the session had been uncomfortable but useful.
story_3_dissimilar: Leah decided to look for a therapist after an argument with her sister. She asked a friend for a recommendation instead of searching for long. She still hesitated before reaching out. The next morning, she booked a first appointment. On the train to the office, she wondered if she should cancel. She arrived for the session on time. At first, she discussed burnout and constant guilt. Later, the therapist asked what she wanted from other people. That topic felt unexpectedly difficult for her. She gave a vague answer and then admitted she did not know. After the appointment, she sat at a cafe before going home. She thought carefully about whether to continue. By evening, she had decided to wait a few days before making another booking.

theme: A person moves into their first apartment without roommates.
core_events: ["signs the lease for the apartment", "packs belongings and arranges the move", "unlocks the new place and brings in boxes or furniture", "discovers an immediate issue like missing supplies or a maintenance problem", "spends the first night settling in alone"]
story_1_anchor: Maya signed the lease for her first apartment on Monday. She packed her clothes, dishes, and books the next day. She arranged for a small moving truck for Saturday morning. On Saturday, she unlocked the apartment door by herself. She carried in her boxes and a used couch. After that, she noticed the kitchen had no cleaning supplies. She went back out to buy paper towels and soap. That night, she sat on the floor and unpacked a few things. She spent her first night there alone and tried to get comfortable.
story_2_similar: Ethan signed the lease for his first place at the start of the week. He spent two evenings boxing up his belongings. He scheduled the move for the weekend. When he arrived, he unlocked the door to the apartment with his new key. He brought in his bed frame, bags, and several boxes. Soon after, he found that the bathroom light did not work. He called the building manager to report it. Later that night, he made his bed and put away some essentials. He spent his first night alone in the apartment.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena signed the lease for her first apartment after work. She bought tape and boxes that same evening. Before she finished packing, she worried about being alone in a new place. The next day, she packed most of her belongings and confirmed the move with a friend who had a van. In the afternoon, she unlocked the apartment and walked through the empty rooms. She carried in boxes, a lamp, and a small table. Right away, she discovered that the refrigerator was not running. She moved her food into a cooler and sent a maintenance request. That night, she stayed there alone and listened to the building sounds while settling in.

theme: A person reconnects with an old friend at a high school reunion.
core_events: ["decides to attend the reunion after debating it", "arrives at the event and recognizes familiar faces", "spots an old friend and starts a conversation", "shares updates about life since school", "leaves with a plan to stay in touch or meet again"]
story_1_anchor: Maya debated for a week about going to her high school reunion. She finally decided to attend. She walked into the hotel ballroom that evening. She recognized several familiar faces from her class. Near the snack table, she noticed her old friend Jenna. She went over and started talking with her. They shared updates about work, family, and where life had taken them since school. At the end of the night, they agreed to meet for coffee the next month and stay in touch.
story_2_similar: Ethan spent several days unsure about the class reunion. In the end, he chose to go. He arrived at the reunion hall on Saturday night. He saw many faces he remembered from school. Across the room, he spotted his old friend Marcus. Ethan walked up and began a conversation with him. They talked about their jobs, their homes, and the years since graduation. Before leaving, they exchanged numbers and made a plan to meet again soon.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena almost skipped her high school reunion because she felt nervous about it. After thinking it over, she decided to attend. She entered the school gym and paused for a moment. She quickly recognized a few former classmates near the door. One familiar face made her think of her old friend Rachel. A little later, she spotted Rachel by the photo display and started a conversation. They spent a long time sharing updates about life since school. When the reunion ended, they promised to keep in touch and plan lunch together.

theme: A person tries gardening for the first time by growing tomatoes on a balcony or patio.
core_events: ["buys tomato seedlings, pots, and soil", "sets up the containers and plants the seedlings", "creates a routine for watering and checking the plants", "deals with a problem like drooping leaves or pests", "picks the first ripe tomato"]
story_1_anchor: Maya decided to try gardening for the first time on her apartment balcony. She went to a garden store and bought tomato seedlings, pots, and soil. She carried everything home and set the pots along the balcony railing. She filled the containers with soil. She planted the tomato seedlings in the pots. She made a simple routine for the plants. She watered them every morning. She also checked the leaves each evening. After a week, some leaves started to droop in the afternoon sun. She moved the pots to a spot with a little shade. She kept watching the plants each day. Later, one tomato turned fully red. Maya picked her first ripe tomato and felt proud.
story_2_similar: Ethan wanted to grow tomatoes for the first time on his small patio. He visited a nursery and bought tomato seedlings, pots, and soil. He brought the supplies home and placed the containers near the patio wall. He added soil to each pot. He planted the seedlings carefully. He set up a daily habit for caring for them. He watered the plants every morning before work. He checked the stems and leaves every night. Soon, he noticed a few drooping leaves during hot weather. He gave the plants shade in the afternoon. He continued his routine for the next few weeks. At last, one tomato became bright red. Ethan picked the first ripe tomato and showed it to his neighbor.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena tried balcony gardening for the first time because she wanted fresh tomatoes. She bought tomato seedlings, pots, and soil at a weekend market. Before planting, she chose the sunniest corner of the balcony. She set the pots there and filled them with soil. She planted the seedlings one by one. On the second day, she saw small holes in a few leaves. She looked closely and found tiny pests. She wiped the leaves and removed the bugs. After that, she started a routine for the plants. She watered them each morning. She checked them again after dinner. For a while, the plants only grew taller. Then the first tomato slowly ripened. Lena picked the first red tomato and tasted it right away.

theme: A person prepares for and takes their driver's license road test.
core_events: ["schedules the road test date", "practices driving with an instructor or family member", "feels nervous while waiting at the testing center", "completes the road test with the examiner", "receives the result and reacts to it"]
story_1_anchor: Maya scheduled her road test for Friday morning. She practiced driving with her father after school for two weeks. She felt nervous while waiting at the testing center. She completed the road test with the examiner. She received the result and smiled because she passed.
story_2_similar: Ethan booked his road test for an early appointment on Tuesday. He practiced driving with an instructor in the days before the test. He felt anxious while sitting in the waiting area at the testing center. He completed the road test with the examiner. He got the result and felt relieved that he passed.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena set a date for her road test at the local testing center. She felt very nervous on the morning of the exam. Before the test day, she practiced driving with her older sister in a quiet neighborhood. She completed the road test with the examiner. She received the result and was upset because she failed.

theme: A person hosts a holiday meal for the first time.
core_events: ["invites guests and plans the menu", "shops for groceries and household supplies", "cooks multiple dishes while managing timing", "handles a kitchen problem such as a delayed dish or missing ingredient", "serves the meal and sees how the gathering goes"]
story_1_anchor: Maya decided to host a holiday meal for the first time. She invited her family and planned a simple menu. The next day, she went to the store for groceries and extra plates. On the holiday morning, she cooked several dishes and watched the clock carefully. One casserole was still cold in the middle, so she had to put it back in the oven. Later, she served the meal to everyone at the table. The gathering went well, and her guests praised the food.
story_2_similar: Ethan was hosting his first holiday dinner at home. He asked his relatives to come over and chose the dishes he wanted to make. After that, he bought the food, napkins, and serving bowls. On the big day, he prepared many recipes and tried to keep the timing under control. He then noticed he was missing butter for the rolls, so he borrowed some from a neighbor. In the evening, he brought out the meal for his guests. The dinner was a success, and people stayed late talking.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena agreed to hold the family holiday meal for the first time. She started cooking early and worked on several dishes at once. Before that weekend, she had invited her cousins and written out a menu. She had also shopped for vegetables, meat, candles, and clean towels. During the cooking, the gravy took much longer than she expected. She served the meal a little late because of that delay. The guests were patient, and the visit still felt warm and happy.

theme: A person loses their wallet and spends the day trying to recover from it.
core_events: ["realizes the wallet is missing", "retraces recent steps and searches likely places", "cancels cards or contacts the bank", "checks with a store, transit office, or lost-and-found", "either recovers the wallet or starts replacing important items"]
story_1_anchor: After lunch, Mia reached for her wallet and saw it was gone. She walked back to the cafe and the bus stop she had used earlier. She looked under the table, around the counter, and along the sidewalk. When she still could not find it, she called her bank and froze her cards. After that, she asked the cafe staff if anyone had turned in a wallet. She also called the city transit lost-and-found office. By evening, nothing had been reported. She started the process of replacing her ID and transit pass.
story_2_similar: In the afternoon, Daniel checked his pocket and realized his wallet was missing. He returned to the bakery and the train platform from his morning errands. He searched the seats, the floor, and the path between both places. Since the wallet did not appear, he contacted his bank and canceled his debit card. Next, he spoke with the bakery cashier about any wallet that had been found. He then called the station lost-and-found desk. No one had it by the end of the day. He began replacing his license and bank cards.
story_3_dissimilar: Late in the day, Rosa noticed that her wallet was not in her bag. She first went back through the park and the pharmacy where she had stopped earlier. She checked the bench, the checkout area, and the parking lot. She then phoned the pharmacy to ask whether a wallet had been turned in. After that, she called the bus company's lost-and-found office. When she still had no answer, she contacted her bank and locked her cards. The next morning, the pharmacy called her back. Her wallet had been found and she picked it up.

theme: A person joins a community choir despite being afraid to sing in front of others.
core_events: ["hears about the choir and decides to try it", "attends the first rehearsal feeling self-conscious", "learns a song and practices with the group", "makes a mistake or feels embarrassed during rehearsal", "performs at a small concert or informal event"]
story_1_anchor: Maya heard about a community choir from her neighbor. She decided to give it a try even though she was scared to sing in front of people. She went to the first rehearsal and felt very self-conscious. She stood in the back and sang quietly. The director taught the group a new song. Maya learned the song and practiced it with everyone else. During rehearsal, she came in at the wrong time and felt embarrassed. She kept going after the mistake. A few weeks later, the choir sang at a small library event. Maya performed with the group and felt proud at the end.
story_2_similar: Elena saw a flyer for a local choir at the community center. She chose to join even though singing in public made her nervous. She attended her first rehearsal and felt awkward right away. She avoided looking at the other singers. The conductor introduced a simple song to the group. Elena learned the song and practiced it with the choir. In one rehearsal, her voice cracked on a high note and she blushed. She stayed for the rest of practice. Later, the choir performed at a small event in the park. Elena sang with them and was glad she had come.
story_3_dissimilar: Jordan heard from a friend that a neighborhood choir needed new members. Jordan decided to try it despite a strong fear of singing in front of others. At home, Jordan worried for days about being judged. Jordan went to the first rehearsal and felt tense and exposed. The choir began working on a short song for an upcoming gathering. Jordan practiced the song with the group but kept the voice very soft. During the next rehearsal, Jordan missed an entry and felt foolish. After that, Jordan practiced the hard part alone at home. Soon the choir sang at an informal café night. Jordan performed with the group and felt less afraid afterward.

theme: A person helps care for a grandparent after a minor surgery.
core_events: ["learns the grandparent will need help during recovery", "drives or accompanies them home after the procedure", "manages meals, medication, or household tasks for them", "handles a tense or emotional moment during recovery", "sees the grandparent regain some independence"]
story_1_anchor: My mother called and told me that Grandpa would need help for a few days after his minor knee surgery. I took the afternoon off so I could be there. After the procedure, I signed his papers and drove him home slowly. That evening, I made him soup and set out his pain pills on time. The next morning, I washed the dishes and took out the trash for him. On the second night, he got upset because he could not get out of bed by himself. I stayed calm and helped him sit up, and then he settled down. By the end of the week, he could walk to the kitchen with his cane and pour his own coffee.
story_2_similar: I found out that my grandmother would need some help while she recovered from a small hip procedure. I arranged my schedule so I could stay with her. When the clinic released her, I walked her to the car and took her home. At home, I cooked simple meals and gave her the medicine when the alarm went off. I also handled the laundry and cleaned the counters each day. One afternoon, she became tearful because she hated asking for help. I listened to her and reminded her that the recovery was temporary. A few days later, she was able to move around the apartment on her own and make herself tea.
story_3_dissimilar: My aunt told me that Grandma would need support after a minor hand surgery. I met her at the outpatient center when the procedure was done. I rode home with her in a taxi and carried her bag inside. During the first day, I changed the bandage supplies on the table and prepared lunch for both of us. I also kept track of her medication times and fed her cat. Before dinner, she insisted on reaching a high shelf and got angry when I stopped her. We argued for a minute, and then she admitted she felt useless. The next morning, she buttoned her sweater by herself. Later that week, she watered her plants without asking me to do it.

theme: A person attends a local protest or civic meeting for the first time about an issue they care about.
core_events: ["decides to show up after following the issue for a while", "travels to the event and takes in the atmosphere", "listens to speeches, discussion, or public comments", "speaks up, signs something, or participates in a visible way", "leaves reflecting on the experience and next steps"]
story_1_anchor: Maya had followed the debate over cuts to the town library for several months. She finally decided to attend a city hall protest for the first time. After work, she walked to the square and noticed handmade signs, neighbors talking, and a tense but hopeful mood. She stood near the steps and listened to speakers explain why the library mattered. Later, the meeting opened for public comments, and she listened to several residents speak. When the sign-up sheet came around, Maya added her name and then gave a short comment about her children using the library. After the event ended, she walked home thinking about how nervous she had been. She decided she would come back to the next meeting and email her council member.
story_2_similar: Jordan had been reading about plans to close a local bus route for a long time. He decided that this time he would go to the neighborhood meeting in person. He took the bus to the community center and looked around at the crowd, the posters, and the folding chairs. He listened as organizers gave short speeches about how the route helped workers and students. He also listened to public comments from riders who depended on the service. When volunteers passed out a petition, Jordan signed it and raised his hand to speak briefly. He left the building feeling more involved than he expected. On the way home, he thought about attending another meeting and bringing a friend.
story_3_dissimilar: Elena had cared about rising water bills for months before she ever joined any public event. She drove to a town council meeting after deciding she could not stay on the sidelines. Before the session started, she noticed police barriers outside, a few chanting protesters, and many older residents waiting at the entrance. Soon she wrote her name on the list for speakers because she was afraid she might lose her nerve later. She then sat down and listened to council members, activists, and homeowners argue about the issue. After her turn at the microphone, she spoke about her fixed budget and asked for clearer billing. She left unsure whether the officials would change anything. Still, she felt proud that she had shown up, and she planned to follow the next vote online.

theme: A person sells handmade crafts at their first weekend market.
core_events: ["applies for a booth and prepares items to sell", "sets prices and packs supplies for the market", "arrives early to set up the table or stall", "interacts with shoppers and makes the first sale", "packs up at the end and counts the day's results"]
story_1_anchor: Maya applied for a booth at the weekend market. She spent the week making candles and knit scarves to sell. On Friday night, she wrote prices on small tags. She packed her tablecloth, cash box, and extra bags for the market. She arrived early on Saturday morning. She set up her table and arranged her crafts in neat rows. She greeted shoppers as they walked by. A woman bought a blue candle, and Maya made her first sale. At the end of the day, she packed up the unsold items. She counted her money and saw that the market had gone well.
story_2_similar: Lena signed up for a booth at her first weekend market. She prepared earrings and soap bars for customers. The night before the event, she decided on prices for each item. She packed boxes, signs, and change for the market. She reached the market early the next morning. She opened her stall and placed everything on the table. She talked with people who stopped to look. One shopper purchased a pair of earrings, and Lena made her first sale. After the market ended, she packed her remaining crafts. She counted the cash and felt happy with the day's results.
story_3_dissimilar: Jordan wanted to try selling handmade crafts at a weekend market. She applied for a booth and waited for approval. She spent several evenings making ceramic magnets and painted cards. Before the market, she packed her display stands, snacks, and wrapping paper. She checked her prices again while sitting in the car. She got to the market very early. She took time to set up the stall because it was her first event. At first, only a few shoppers stopped. Later, one man bought a painted card, and Jordan made her first sale. Near closing time, she packed everything into plastic bins. At home, she counted the money and saw that she had earned less than she hoped.

theme: A person repairs a strained relationship with a neighbor after an argument over noise.
core_events: ["has a conflict with the neighbor about loud noise", "spends time feeling upset and avoiding contact", "decides to start a calm conversation or bring an apology", "talks through the problem and listens to the neighbor's side", "agrees on a new understanding or boundary"]
story_1_anchor: I argued with my neighbor because my music was too loud at night. After that, I felt upset for several days. I avoided seeing him in the hallway. Then I decided to knock on his door and apologize calmly. We talked about the noise problem. I listened while he explained that it was keeping his baby awake. In the end, we agreed that I would keep the volume low after 9 p.m.
story_2_similar: I had a conflict with my neighbor over the loud TV in my apartment. For a few days, I stayed irritated about the argument. I kept my distance and did not speak to her. Later, I chose to start a calm conversation and say I was sorry. We discussed what had happened. I listened as she told me the sound was reaching her bedroom wall. After that, we agreed that I would use headphones late in the evening.
story_3_dissimilar: My neighbor got angry when I played drums too loudly one weekend. I spent the next week feeling bad about the fight. I stayed out of his way and stopped greeting him. Before speaking, I thought about why he was so frustrated. Then I went over and offered an apology. We sat down and talked through the issue. I listened to his side and heard that he works early mornings. We agreed on quiet hours for practice, and things became easier between us.

theme: A person leaves an office job to start a small home bakery.
core_events: ["decides to resign from the office job", "tests several recipes for a signature menu", "gets permits and sets up a home kitchen workspace", "announces the bakery on social media", "fulfills the first round of customer orders"]
story_1_anchor: Maya decided to resign from her office job. She wanted to turn her baking hobby into a small business. She tested several recipes for a signature menu. She compared cakes, cookies, and bread. She chose the items that tasted best and were easy to make well. She got the needed permits for a home bakery. She set up a workspace in her kitchen. She bought racks, trays, and storage containers. She announced the bakery on social media. She posted photos of her menu and opening date. Soon, she fulfilled the first round of customer orders. She packed each order carefully and delivered them on time.
story_2_similar: Elena decided to leave her office job. She had been thinking about running a bakery from home. She tested many recipes for her signature menu. She tried different frostings, fillings, and doughs. She kept the products that customers would likely remember. She applied for permits for her home business. She organized a baking area in her kitchen. She added shelves, mixing tools, and labeled bins. She announced her new bakery on social media. She shared pictures and invited friends to place orders. After that, she completed the first batch of customer orders. She boxed the pastries neatly and handed them out that weekend.
story_3_dissimilar: Nina decided to quit her office job. She spent a few days thinking about what kind of bakery she wanted. She tested several recipes for a signature menu. She focused more on pies than on bread. She announced the bakery on social media early. She wanted to see if anyone would be interested. Then she got the permits for a home bakery. She set up her kitchen workspace after that. She cleared one counter and added basic baking supplies. At the end of the week, she fulfilled her first customer orders. The small launch went well, even though the setup was simple.

theme: Someone adopts a shy rescue dog and helps it settle into daily life.
core_events: ["visits an animal shelter and meets the dog", "brings the dog home with basic supplies", "struggles through the dog's nervous first week", "starts a consistent walking and training routine", "sees the dog relax during a trip to the park"]
story_1_anchor: Maya visited an animal shelter on Saturday. She met a shy brown dog that stayed at the back of the kennel. She decided to adopt him. She brought the dog home with a leash, a bed, food bowls, and a bag of kibble. During the first week, the dog trembled at noises and hid under the table. Maya had trouble getting him to eat and sleep calmly. After that, she began a regular routine of morning walks and short training sessions. She practiced the same simple commands each day. Two weeks later, she took him to the park. There, she saw him relax on the grass and wag his tail at a passing dog.
story_2_similar: Evan went to the local shelter after work. He met a quiet rescue dog that would not come forward at first. He chose to take her home. He arrived home with the dog, a crate, a collar, some toys, and dog food. The first week was difficult because the dog paced at night and flinched at sudden sounds. Evan struggled to help her feel safe in the apartment. The next week, he started a steady schedule of walks and basic training. He repeated the same route and the same cues every day. Soon after, he brought her to a nearby park. At the park, he noticed that she lay down calmly and watched people without fear.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena stopped by an animal shelter and met a small rescue dog with nervous eyes. She adopted the dog that day. She took the dog home with a borrowed crate, a soft blanket, and a few basic supplies. The first days were tense, and the dog stayed close to the wall. Before the week ended, Lena tried short walks outside to build a routine. She added simple training at home after each walk. Even with that plan, the dog still startled easily during the first week. At the end of the week, Lena took the dog to a quiet park early in the morning. She saw the dog loosen his posture and sniff around without pulling back.

theme: A college student prepares for and gives a major class presentation.
core_events: ["gets assigned the presentation topic", "researches sources and outlines the talk", "practices the presentation several times", "deals with nerves right before class", "delivers the presentation and gets feedback"]
story_1_anchor: In her history class, Maya got assigned a topic for a major presentation. She went to the library and researched sources for it. She wrote a clear outline for her talk. During the week, she practiced the presentation several times in her dorm room. Right before class, she felt very nervous and took a few deep breaths. Then she gave the presentation to her class. Afterward, her professor and classmates gave her helpful feedback.
story_2_similar: Ethan was assigned a presentation topic in his sociology course. He looked up articles and books about the subject. He made an outline to organize his main points. Over the next few days, he practiced the presentation again and again. Just before class started, he got nervous and tried to stay calm. He delivered the presentation in front of everyone. When he finished, he received feedback from the teacher and the other students.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena received a topic for an important class presentation in her biology course. She felt pressure early because the grade was a big part of the class. Before she finished planning, she practiced once to see what she already knew. Then she researched sources and took notes from them. After that, she made an outline for the talk. On presentation day, she practiced several more times in the hallway. Right before class, her nerves got worse and her hands shook. She still delivered the presentation to the class. In the end, she got mixed feedback, but the teacher said her main ideas were clear.

theme: A person trains for and completes their first long-distance bike ride.
core_events: ["signs up for the cycling event", "buys or tunes up a bike for training", "builds a weekly riding schedule", "pushes through a difficult long practice ride", "finishes the event on race day"]
story_1_anchor: Maya signed up for her first long-distance cycling event. She took her old bike to a shop for a full tune-up. She made a weekly riding schedule and put it on her fridge. A few weeks later, she struggled through a very long practice ride in strong wind. She kept going and finished the training route. On race day, she completed the event and felt proud.
story_2_similar: Ethan registered for his first long-distance bike ride. He bought a better bike so he could train safely. He wrote out a weekly plan for his rides. During one long practice ride, his legs hurt and he wanted to stop. He pushed through the hard training ride and got home tired. On the day of the event, he reached the finish line.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena wanted to prove she could handle a long bike event. She bought a used road bike and started riding short distances. After that, she signed up for the event. She later set a weekly training schedule for herself. One weekend, she faced a difficult long practice ride with steep hills. She got through that ride with several rest breaks. On race day, she finished her first long-distance bike ride.

theme: Someone travels alone to a new city for a weekend and learns to enjoy solo travel.
core_events: ["books tickets and a place to stay", "arrives in the city and navigates to the hotel", "explores a neighborhood alone for the first time", "handles a small travel problem like getting lost or missing a train", "ends the trip feeling more confident"]
story_1_anchor: Maya decided to spend a weekend alone in a new city. She booked a train ticket and reserved a small hotel room. She arrived on Friday afternoon. She used a map on her phone to get to the hotel. After checking in, she walked around a nearby neighborhood by herself for the first time. At first she felt awkward, but she kept going. The next morning, she took the wrong street and got lost for a while. She stopped at a cafe and asked for directions. She found her way back and continued her day. By Sunday evening, she felt calm and capable. She went home more confident about traveling alone.
story_2_similar: Ethan planned a solo weekend in a city he had never visited. He bought his bus ticket and booked a room in a guesthouse. He reached the city on Saturday morning. He followed the street signs and navigated to his hotel. Later, he explored a local neighborhood on his own for the first time. He noticed shops, parks, and quiet side streets. That evening, he missed the right tram stop and had to walk back. He checked the transit map and corrected his route. After that, he felt less nervous. He ended the trip with more confidence about solo travel.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena wanted to test herself with a solo weekend in a different city. She reserved a cheap hostel bed and bought a train ticket. She arrived early and felt unsure right away. She explored a busy neighborhood alone before she fully relaxed. She liked choosing her own pace. Later, she tried to reach her hotel and took a confusing bus route. She got off at the wrong stop and wandered for a few minutes. She then asked a passerby for help and found the hostel. The small mistake embarrassed her at first. By the end of the weekend, she felt proud and more comfortable being on her own.

theme: A person discovers they need glasses and adjusts to wearing them.
core_events: ["notices recurring trouble reading signs or screens", "schedules and attends an eye exam", "chooses a pair of frames", "picks up the new glasses and tries them on", "gets used to wearing them in daily routines"]
story_1_anchor: Maya kept having trouble reading road signs while driving to work. She also had to hold her laptop closer to see the words clearly. She scheduled an eye exam at a local clinic. She went to the appointment the next week. The doctor tested her vision and said she needed glasses. Maya looked at several frame options in the shop. She chose a simple black pair that fit her face well. A few days later, she picked up her new glasses. She put them on in the store and noticed everything looked sharper. At first, wearing them all day felt strange. Soon she got used to wearing them while driving, working, and shopping.
story_2_similar: Ethan started missing words on street signs during his morning commute. He also struggled to read text on his computer screen at home. He made an appointment for an eye exam. He attended the exam after work on Thursday. The optometrist checked his eyes and told him he needed glasses. Ethan tried on different frames near the front counter. He picked a light gray pair that felt comfortable. Later that week, he returned to pick up the finished glasses. He tried them on right away and saw the room more clearly. The glasses felt unusual on his face at first. After some days, he adjusted to wearing them during errands, work, and reading.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena often squinted at menu boards and bus signs. She ignored the problem for a while because she thought she was just tired. After struggling to read her tablet screen one evening, she decided to get her eyes checked. She scheduled an eye exam for the following Monday. She visited the eye doctor and completed the exam. The doctor said glasses would help her see better. Lena cared a lot about how the frames looked. She spent extra time comparing colors and shapes. In the end, she chose a round brown pair. When the glasses were ready, she went back to the store to collect them. She tried them on and felt surprised by how crisp everything seemed. She wore them only for short periods at first. Gradually, she became comfortable using them in her daily routine.

theme: Two siblings work together to clean out their late grandparent's house.
core_events: ["return to the house with boxes and supplies", "sort belongings room by room", "pause over a sentimental item that brings back memories", "disagree briefly about what to keep or donate", "finish the cleanup and lock up the house"]
story_1_anchor: Maya and her brother Eli came back to their late grandmother's house with boxes, gloves, and trash bags. They started in the kitchen and sorted her things into keep, donate, and throw away piles. They moved through the house one room at a time and kept sorting. In the bedroom, Maya found their grandmother's old recipe book. She stopped and remembered baking with her at the table. Eli wanted to donate more of the dishes, but Maya wanted to keep several sets. They talked for a minute and agreed on saving only a few. By evening, they had cleared the rooms and loaded the car. Maya turned off the lights and locked the house before they left.
story_2_similar: Nina and her brother Sam returned to their late grandfather's house carrying boxes, cleaning spray, and markers. They began in the living room and sorted his belongings into boxes for keeping, giving away, and trash. They went room by room and continued the same work. In the hall closet, Sam found an old fishing hat. He paused and thought about summer trips with their grandfather. Nina wanted to keep a stack of blankets, but Sam said most of them should be donated. They argued briefly and then chose a small number to save. At the end of the day, the house was cleaned out and the donation boxes were packed. Sam locked the front door as they walked away.
story_3_dissimilar: Leah and her brother Jonah drove to their late grandmother's house with empty bins, tape, and rags. Leah looked around the quiet entryway before they began. They sorted the downstairs rooms first and made separate piles for family keepsakes, donations, and trash. In the dining room, Jonah picked up their grandmother's music box. He stood still for a moment and remembered hearing it after dinner when they were children. They carried on and sorted the upstairs rooms after that. Near the end, they disagreed about an old armchair because Jonah wanted to keep it and Leah wanted to donate it. They settled the question by calling their mother. After that, they finished the last bags, closed the windows, and locked up the house.

theme: Someone learns to cook one meaningful family dish from scratch.
core_events: ["asks a relative for the recipe and advice", "shops for the specific ingredients", "makes mistakes during the first attempt", "tries the dish again with adjustments", "serves the finished meal to family or friends"]
story_1_anchor: Maya wanted to learn her grandmother's chicken soup from scratch. She called her grandmother and asked for the recipe. She also asked for advice about the broth and noodles. The next day, she went to the market for a whole chicken, carrots, celery, onions, and fresh parsley. She made the soup that evening. She added too much salt and cooked the noodles too long. She was disappointed, but she wrote down what went wrong. Two days later, she tried the soup again. She used less salt and cooked the noodles for less time. The soup tasted warm and balanced. She served big bowls to her parents and brother. They smiled because it tasted like home.
story_2_similar: Ethan decided to make his aunt's beef stew on his own. He visited his aunt and asked her for the full recipe. He asked her for extra tips about browning the meat and thickening the sauce. After work, he shopped for beef, potatoes, onions, carrots, and rosemary. He cooked the stew that night in a large pot. He burned some onions and made the sauce too thin. He felt frustrated, so he looked over his notes again. That weekend, he made the stew a second time. He lowered the heat and added less broth. The stew came out rich and hearty. He served it to his sister and two friends. They said it reminded them of family dinners.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena had always wanted to learn her father's special rice pudding from scratch. Before she cooked, she asked her father for the recipe. She asked him how to keep the milk from scorching. She bought rice, milk, sugar, cinnamon, and raisins from a small grocery store. She told her cousin she hoped to serve the dessert at Sunday dinner. On her first try, she cooked it too fast. The bottom burned and the pudding turned thick and lumpy. She almost gave up after that mistake. The next afternoon, she tried again with a lower flame and more stirring. The pudding came out smooth and soft. On Sunday, she served bowls to her father, cousin, and neighbor. Her father said the flavor was very close to his mother's version.

theme: A person realizes they are overspending and creates a working budget.
core_events: ["checks bank statements and sees the problem", "lists monthly expenses and debts", "cuts a few discretionary purchases", "sets up a budgeting system or app", "makes it through the first month on the new plan"]
story_1_anchor: Maya checked her bank statements at the end of the month. She saw that she had been spending more than she expected. She wrote down her monthly bills. She also listed her credit card debt and loan payments. She stopped buying coffee on the way to work. She also paused her movie subscription. Then she set up a budgeting app on her phone. She gave each category a spending limit. During the first month, she followed the plan closely. She made it to the end of the month without overspending.
story_2_similar: Jordan looked through his bank statements one weekend. He realized his spending had gotten out of control. He made a list of his regular monthly expenses. He added his debt payments to the list. He decided to cut takeout meals. He also canceled one streaming service. After that, he started using a budgeting app. He entered limits for rent, food, and other categories. In the first month, he checked the app often. He finished the month within his new budget.
story_3_dissimilar: Elena checked her bank statements after her rent payment cleared. She noticed that too much money was disappearing each month. She set up a simple budgeting spreadsheet right away. She wanted a clear place to track every dollar. Next, she wrote out her monthly expenses. She added her store card balance and car loan bill. Then she cut back on clothes shopping. She also stopped ordering dessert with lunch. The first month felt strict, but she stayed on the plan. She got through the month without going over budget.

theme: Someone moves into their first apartment and figures out living alone.
core_events: ["signs the lease and gets the keys", "packs belongings and completes the move", "discovers something missing or broken in the apartment", "buys basic household essentials", "spends the first comfortable evening in the new place"]
story_1_anchor: Maya signed the lease for her first apartment. She got the keys from the landlord that afternoon. The next day, she packed her clothes, dishes, and books into boxes. She moved everything into the apartment with help from her brother. After the boxes were inside, she saw that the kitchen light was broken. She reported the problem and then went to a store nearby. She bought soap, toilet paper, a shower curtain, and a few groceries. That night, she unpacked the bed and made the room feel calm. She spent her first comfortable evening alone in her new place.
story_2_similar: Jordan signed the lease on his first apartment. He received the keys right after the paperwork was finished. On moving day, he packed his things into bags and boxes. He carried his belongings into the apartment with a rented van. Once he looked around, he noticed that the bathroom sink was missing a stopper. He told the building manager about it. Later, he went shopping for paper towels, cleaning spray, dishes, and food. In the evening, he set up his bed and sat down to relax. He enjoyed his first comfortable evening in the apartment by himself.
story_3_dissimilar: Elena signed the lease for her first apartment. She picked up the keys and unlocked the door by herself. Before moving the last boxes, she noticed that one window blind was broken. She felt stressed, but she decided to keep going. She packed the rest of her belongings into her car. She completed the move after two long trips across town. After that, she bought a lamp, a trash can, towels, and some breakfast food. She called maintenance about the blind when she got back. Later that night, she ate on the floor and finally felt at home. It was her first comfortable evening living alone.

theme: A person reconnects with an old friend at a high school reunion.
core_events: ["hesitates but decides to attend the reunion", "arrives and recognizes familiar faces", "starts talking with the old friend again", "shares updates about the years apart", "makes plans to stay in touch after the event"]
story_1_anchor: Maya was unsure about going to her high school reunion. She hesitated for several days, but then she decided to attend. She walked into the banquet hall on Saturday evening. She looked around and recognized many familiar faces from her class. After a few minutes, she saw Daniel near the refreshment table. She went over and started talking with him again. They spoke about where they had lived and worked since graduation. They shared updates about their families and daily lives. Before the reunion ended, they agreed to keep in touch. They exchanged phone numbers and planned to meet for coffee the next month.
story_2_similar: Lena almost skipped her high school reunion. She paused at the last minute, but she chose to go. She arrived at the hotel ballroom that night. She quickly noticed several familiar faces from school. Soon she spotted her old friend Marcus by the wall. She walked up to him and began talking with him again. They talked about the years they had spent apart. They shared news about jobs, moves, and relationships. At the end of the event, they decided to stay in contact. They traded numbers and made a plan to have lunch soon.
story_3_dissimilar: Erin did not want to attend her high school reunion at first. She hesitated because she felt nervous, but she finally decided to go. When she entered the hall, she recognized old classmates almost right away. Seeing those familiar faces made her feel more comfortable. Later, she noticed her old friend Chloe near the photo display. Erin started talking with Chloe again after many years. They first laughed about school memories for a while. Then they shared updates about the time they had spent apart. They talked about work, family, and new cities. After the reunion, they made plans to stay in touch. They connected on social media and agreed to call each other the next week.

theme: Someone prepares a small backyard garden for the first growing season.
core_events: ["chooses a spot and sketches a garden plan", "buys soil, tools, and seedlings or seeds", "spends a day clearing and planting the beds", "deals with an early setback like pests or drooping plants", "harvests the first usable vegetables or herbs"]
story_1_anchor: In early spring, Maya picked a sunny corner of the backyard for a small garden. She drew a simple plan on paper and marked where each crop would go. The next weekend, she went to a garden store for bags of soil, a hand trowel, and tomato and basil seedlings. After that, she spent a full Saturday pulling weeds and turning the ground into neat beds. She planted the seedlings and watered them well. A few days later, some leaves had holes from insects and one tomato plant drooped. She removed the worst leaves and used a mild spray to protect the plants. By the start of summer, she clipped her first basil stems and picked two ripe tomatoes.
story_2_similar: At the start of the season, Lena chose a bright patch near the fence for her first backyard garden. She made a small sketch so she knew where the herbs and vegetables should be planted. Soon after, she bought fresh soil, a shovel, and packs of lettuce and parsley seedlings. On her day off, she cleared grass from the area and shaped several small beds. She set the seedlings in the soil and gave them a deep watering. In the first week, tiny pests chewed some leaves and a few plants looked limp. She checked the garden each morning and treated the problem before it spread. Later, she cut her first lettuce leaves and gathered a handful of parsley.
story_3_dissimilar: Omar wanted a simple backyard garden for his first growing season. Before he bought anything, he walked around the yard and chose a spot that got sun most of the afternoon. He spent time thinking about easy crops for that space. The next day, he bought seed packets, potting soil, and a hoe. That evening, he drew a rough garden plan after looking at the yard again. A week later, he used a whole Sunday to clear the patch and make planting rows. He sowed radish and dill seeds and watered the ground. Soon after, several seedlings drooped during a hot spell. He added shade cloth and watered earlier in the day. Not long after that, he pulled a few radishes and cut some dill for dinner.

theme: A person studies for and retakes a driving test after failing once.
core_events: ["fails the first driving test", "identifies the mistakes that caused the failure", "practices the weak skills with an instructor or family member", "returns to the testing center for the retake", "receives the new result"]
story_1_anchor: Maya took her driving test and failed the first time. She read the score sheet and identified the mistakes that caused the failure. She had trouble with parallel parking and checking mirrors during turns. She practiced those weak skills with her uncle for two weeks. She then returned to the testing center for the retake. She received the new result and passed the test.
story_2_similar: Jordan went to the road test and did not pass on the first attempt. Afterward, he reviewed the examiner's notes and identified the mistakes behind the failure. He saw that lane changes and backing into a space were his weak points. He practiced those skills with a driving instructor every evening. Later, he returned to the testing center for the retake. He received the new result and passed.
story_3_dissimilar: Elena failed her first driving test on a rainy morning. She felt upset and talked about the test with her mother that night. The next day, she identified the mistakes that had led to the failure. She noticed that she hesitated at stop signs and steered badly while parking. Before the retake, she returned to the testing center once to check the route area. She then practiced the weak skills with her older sister for several days. A week later, she returned to the testing center for the retake. She received the new result and failed again.

theme: Someone hosts their first holiday dinner for extended family.
core_events: ["invites relatives and plans the menu", "shops for groceries and decorations", "starts cooking and managing the house setup", "handles a last-minute problem in the kitchen", "sits down with everyone for the meal"]
story_1_anchor: Maya decided to host her first holiday dinner for her extended family. She called her relatives and invited them to her apartment. She planned a simple menu for the evening. The next day, she went to the grocery store for food. She also bought candles and a table runner for the dining room. On the holiday morning, she started cooking early. She arranged chairs, plates, and serving dishes around the house. In the afternoon, the oven stopped heating for a few minutes. She moved one dish to the stove and finished the meal there. That evening, everyone arrived and sat down together for dinner.
story_2_similar: Lena was nervous about hosting her first holiday meal for the whole family. She sent invitations to her aunts, uncles, and cousins. She wrote out the dishes she wanted to serve. Later, she shopped for vegetables, meat, and dessert items. She picked up a few decorations for the table and entryway. On the big day, she began cooking in the morning. She cleaned the living room and set the table for her guests. Just before people came, she dropped the gravy and made a quick new batch. At dinner time, the family gathered and sat down for the meal.
story_3_dissimilar: Nora agreed to host her first holiday dinner for her extended family this year. She spent the morning setting up the house with extra chairs and clean linens. After that, she checked her guest list and invited the relatives who had not replied yet. She then chose the dishes she would make for the dinner. In the afternoon, she went out to buy groceries. She added flowers and napkins to the cart for decoration. Back home, she started cooking the main dishes. Near the end, she realized she had burned the rolls in the kitchen. She warmed bread from the freezer instead. Soon after, everyone sat down together for the holiday meal.

theme: A person deals with a phone breaking right before an important week.
core_events: ["drops the phone and realizes it no longer works properly", "tries temporary fixes like charging, restarting, or borrowing a device", "backs up or attempts to recover important information", "visits a repair shop or store to decide on repair versus replacement", "sets up the working phone again"]
story_1_anchor: The night before a very busy week, Maya dropped her phone on the kitchen floor. She picked it up and saw that the screen was glitching and the phone no longer worked properly. She plugged it in to charge and hoped that would help. She restarted it several times, but the problem stayed. She borrowed her sister's old phone for the next morning. She tried to back up her calendar, notes, and contacts from the damaged phone. She recovered some files, but a few items would not copy. On Monday afternoon, she went to a phone repair shop. She asked about the cost of fixing it and the price of a replacement. She decided to buy a replacement because her week was too important to risk delays. That evening, she set up the working phone again. She signed back into her accounts and checked that her schedule was there.
story_2_similar: Right before an important week at work, Daniel dropped his phone in the driveway. He noticed that the display flickered and the phone did not work correctly anymore. First, he connected it to a charger to see if it would respond. Next, he turned it off and on, but nothing improved. He borrowed a spare device from his roommate so he could stay reachable. After that, he attempted to back up his messages, contacts, and photos from the broken phone. He managed to save most of the information, though some recent pictures were missing. The next day, he visited a store that handled phone repairs. He compared the repair option with the cost of getting a new phone. He chose a replacement so he would have something dependable for the week. Later that night, he set up the working phone again. He restored his data and tested his apps before bed.
story_3_dissimilar: On Sunday, Lena was getting ready for an important week when she dropped her phone on the sidewalk. She quickly realized that it no longer worked properly because calls kept failing and the screen froze. She first tried to recover her contact list and work notes because she was worried about Monday. Some of the backup worked, but part of her recent data was lost. She then borrowed her father's spare phone so she would have a way to communicate. She also tried simple fixes on the broken phone, including charging it and restarting it. On Tuesday, she went to a mall kiosk and then a repair store for advice. She learned that a repair would take several days, so she chose a replacement instead. After she got home, she set up the working phone again. She reinstalled her essential apps and checked her calendar for the rest of the week.

theme: Someone joins a community choir despite being nervous about singing in public.
core_events: ["sees an announcement and signs up for choir practice", "attends the first rehearsal and feels intimidated", "learns the songs over several practices", "builds rapport with other choir members", "performs at the first public concert"]
story_1_anchor: Maya saw a flyer for the town choir at the library. She liked singing at home, but she felt nervous about singing in front of people. She signed up for choir practice anyway. She went to the first rehearsal the next week. The room was full of confident voices, and she felt intimidated. She kept coming back to practice. She learned the songs bit by bit over several weeks. She started talking with the other choir members during breaks. She built friendly rapport with the group. At the end of the season, the choir gave its first public concert for her. She stood on stage and performed with them.
story_2_similar: Elena noticed an announcement for a community choir on a cafe bulletin board. She had always been shy about public singing. She put her name down for the choir practice. She attended the first rehearsal a few days later. Hearing the stronger singers around her made her feel intimidated. She returned for the next practices. She learned the concert songs across several rehearsals. She chatted with other members before and after practice. Over time, she built rapport with them. Later, the choir held her first public concert with the group. She sang in front of the audience that evening.
story_3_dissimilar: Jordan was nervous about singing where others could hear. One afternoon, Jordan saw an announcement for the neighborhood choir. Jordan decided to sign up for choir practice. At the first rehearsal, Jordan felt intimidated by the experienced singers. Jordan almost stayed quiet for the whole session. After that, Jordan practiced the choir pieces over several meetings. The songs slowly became familiar. Jordan began to recognize people in the group. Small conversations helped Jordan build rapport with other choir members. By concert week, Jordan felt less afraid than before. Jordan then performed at the first public concert with the choir.

theme: A person prepares for a medical procedure and recovers afterward.
core_events: ["meets with the doctor and schedules the procedure", "follows the pre-procedure instructions", "arrives at the clinic or hospital on the day", "rests and manages discomfort during recovery", "returns for a follow-up appointment"]
story_1_anchor: Maya met with her doctor to talk about her knee procedure. She scheduled the procedure for the next month. Before the date, she followed the instructions from the clinic. She stopped eating after midnight and took only the medicines she was allowed to use. On the morning of the procedure, she arrived at the hospital early. Afterward, she rested at home and managed her discomfort with pain medicine and ice. A week later, she returned for a follow-up appointment.
story_2_similar: Ethan saw his doctor to discuss a minor stomach procedure. He set a date for the procedure before leaving the office. In the days before it, he followed the pre-procedure directions carefully. He avoided certain foods and stopped drinking water at the required time. On the day itself, he got to the clinic with his sister. During recovery, he stayed in bed and handled the soreness with the prescribed medicine. Later, he went back for his follow-up visit.
story_3_dissimilar: Lena met her doctor and arranged a date for a wrist procedure. She felt nervous while waiting for the day. She arrived at the clinic early on the morning of the procedure. Before that day, she had followed the preparation rules from the doctor. After the procedure, she spent several days resting on the couch. She used cold packs to ease the discomfort. At the end of the week, she returned for a follow-up appointment.

theme: Someone helps a younger family member apply to college.
core_events: ["talks through school options and deadlines", "visits campuses or researches programs together", "works on essays and application materials", "submits the applications before the deadline", "opens an admission decision with the family member"]
story_1_anchor: My niece asked me to help her with college applications. We sat at the kitchen table and talked through school choices and the deadlines for each one. The next weekend, we visited two campuses and compared the programs she liked. After that, we worked on her essays and the rest of the application materials. We checked everything twice and submitted the applications before the deadline. A month later, I sat with her when she opened an admission decision on her laptop.
story_2_similar: My younger cousin wanted support while applying to college. I went over different schools with him and listed the due dates on a calendar. Then we researched programs together and looked at virtual campus tours. Later, we revised his essay drafts and finished the application forms. We sent in the applications before any deadline passed. In the spring, I was beside him when he opened an admission decision email.
story_3_dissimilar: My nephew was nervous about applying to college, so I offered to help. First, we looked at several program websites together and read about majors he might study. After that, we talked about which schools fit him best and wrote down the deadlines. Then I helped him shape his essays and gather his application materials. We submitted the applications before the final due date. That evening, he opened an admission decision with me and his parents in the room.

theme: A person decides to commute by bus for the first time after years of driving.
core_events: ["looks up routes, fares, and schedules", "leaves early for the first bus commute", "makes a mistake or gets confused during the trip", "adjusts the routine for the next few days", "settles into a workable public transit habit"]
